We've now worked through the whole shape of the app together, including the rough edges. Here's everything that's settled:

**The everyday flow**
- **Save a link in one step** — paste it, and the title, description, and icon are filled in for you.
- **Tag it** — add tags one at a time, with suggestions so you reuse names instead of inventing new ones; remove a tag with its ×.
- **Write your own note** on any link — the private reminder only you'd think of.
- **Keep a reading list** you opt into deliberately — saving alone doesn't clutter it; you add the things you actually mean to read, and press **Done** to clear them off while keeping the link saved.
- **Find anything again** — search across the title, description, tags, full web address, and your notes, and click any tag to filter, combining the two to narrow down.
- **Remove** a link, with a confirmation so nothing vanishes by accident.

**The rough edges we agreed on**
- If a page's details can't be read automatically, it still saves — showing the address, letting you add a title (and optionally a description) yourself.
- Saving the same link twice takes you to the one you already have instead of duplicating it; typing non-link text is gently blocked.
- Empty screens (first run, empty reading list, no search matches) greet you with a calm one-line prompt, not a blank void.

**Noted for later, not now:** performance/paging tuning for very large collections, whether your links sync across devices, export/backup, and a few smaller refinements.

That's **9 settled behaviours**. This is the scope I'd build.

**May I switch from exploring to actually implementing this app?** Once you say go, I'll change roles from facilitator to builder and start construction against exactly this agreed scope — and I won't change that scope without checking with you.
